# Independent audit: small third fiber with two equal-volume simplices



## Geometric normalization and fixed credits

The continuous affine normalization multiplies every fiber's intrinsic volume by the same determinant. The shear \(x\mapsto x+zp_0\) sends the endpoint fibers to \(A-p_0,C+p_0\), leaves the middle simplex fixed, preserves every integer base, and merely changes the arbitrary integer tilt. The inclusions \(C\subset2B\), \(A\subset2(B-B)\), and the radius \(R=2\sqrt d\) follow exactly. Neither endpoint is assumed to lie in \(B\).

The stochastic matrix has determinant \(2^{-d}\). Replacing one row by the all-row sum and then centering the other rows is determinant preserving. The exponent yielding the \(j\)-th row-maximum margin is correct, with \(j=\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil\ge2\). The fixed subsets use half the guaranteed coordinate excess; their indicators therefore have pointwise multiplicity at least \(j\), giving \(\bar c\ge ja/N\). Varying the selected indices with the point of \(A\) is legitimate.

The endpoint-credit argument has the correct signs for both endpoint thresholds. Its homothetic copy has volume \(V(r^{1/d})^d=a\), because the root note uses \(r=a/V\). Under its closed smallness conditions the perturbation error is at most \(3\delta/4\), leaving a strict \(\delta/4\) margin. This applies to all integer tilts and does not require the small fiber to have small diameter. These conclusions agree with the separately audited robust-credit note.

## Chosen point, one-vertex caps, and perturbation constants

The barycentric definition sums to one, and \(r\le\Gamma/(4d)<\Gamma\) makes every coordinate strictly positive. Its continuous displacement is at most \(\sqrt d\,r/(N\Gamma)\), since the coordinates corresponding to the nonzero vertices are the Euclidean coordinates in the standard simplex.

For a cap with exactly one strictly positive vertex, its intersection is precisely the simplex formed by the incident edge intersections, including possible other vertices on the cut. The identity \(\sum_{k\ne i}\lambda_k(y)/t_k=1\) gives the product lower bound in equation (3) by AM–GM. I independently derived this in `candidate c71e38de38f9f3c8`.

The root note's sign-stability estimate is valid: the combined angular and center perturbation is bounded by

\[
 \frac{\sqrt2}{8N\sqrt d}+\frac1{4N\sqrt d}
          <\frac1{2N\sqrt d}.
\]

The negative centroid margin of every other vertex is at least \(1/(N\sqrt d)\) in absolute value. All these vertices therefore remain strictly negative. The interior barycentric identity then forces the remaining vertex to be strictly positive. The two requirements in the definition of \(\eta\) simultaneously provide endpoint credit and this stable vertex sign pattern.

The finite product remainder has the correct sign and coefficient \(E_d=2^d-d-1\). The credit cancels the linear deficit \(c_i-\bar c\), and \(r\le\Gamma k_d/(2E_d)\) leaves the stated positive excess \(k_da/2\) above the required mass. No unquantified Taylor term remains.

## Attained far-direction gap and threshold sensitivity

The only external geometric input is classical continuous Grünbaum with its equality case, as expressly recorded in `candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c`. For a simplex, an equality pyramid apex must be an extreme point, hence a vertex; all the other vertices determine the opposite facet. Thus its equality directions are exactly the finitely many oriented \(\theta_i\).

The normalized centroid cap function is continuous on the unit sphere because every hyperplane is volume null. The closed complement of the open \(\eta\)-neighborhoods is compact and disjoint from the equality directions, so the minimum \(G_d\) is attained and strictly positive. It is nonempty for every \(d\ge2\): the supplied direction \(-e_1\) has the stated distances. Its distance to \(\theta_0\) is at least \(\sqrt{2-\sqrt2}>1/2\), whereas \(\eta<1/2\). The other distances are even larger.

The section-area bound \(\omega_{d-1}\) follows because the standard simplex lies inside the unit ball. Division by \(V=1/d!\) yields exactly the normalized threshold Lipschitz constant \(L_d=d!\omega_{d-1}\). Moving the through-point threshold from \(g\) to \(y\) changes it by at most \(|y-g|\); its direction and arbitrary integer tilt do not affect the middle-fiber bound. The condition \(r\le G_d/(2Q_d)\) leaves a strict positive excess above \(\Gamma(V+a/2)\).

The constant \(G_d\) is an attained minimum over the one fixed standard simplex, rather than a claimed closed-form elementary constant. This is sufficient for a positive constant depending only on \(d\); the note does not use any unknown mixed-depth extremizer in defining it.

## Exhaustion of halfspaces and exact scope

The two directional cases exhaust all nonzero continuous normals, including the shared neighborhood boundaries. Every such ambient cap boundary has zero \(d\)-volume in each full-dimensional fiber. Purely integer normals are checked separately: their closed through-point caps have masses \(2V\) and \(V+a\), with the full boundary middle fiber retained. Both satisfy the desired bound. Any containing halfspace contains its parallel through-point halfspace, so no cap with a nonincident boundary is omitted.

The convex hull has exactly the three specified integer fibers. In particular the only new endpoint interpolation at base zero is \((A+C)/2\), already inside \(B\). The full-dimensionality and the restrictions \(d\ge2\), \(a>0\), equal large volumes, and simplex shapes are all stated and used consistently. No conclusion about any excluded configuration is inferred.

Exact arithmetic checks for the elementary constants are in `supporting computation verify_small_third_fiber_simplex_audit.py`. They supplement the proof of the compact positive gap rather than numerically estimating it.
